html:
The Treaty of London of 1839 settled the break between Belgium and the Netherlands, and in doing so split Luxembourg in two.

After the Belgian Revolution of 1830 most of Luxembourg had sided with Belgium. The treaty gave the French-speaking west to Belgium, where it is still the Province of Luxembourg. The German-speaking east stayed a grand duchy ruled by the Dutch king and remained in the German Confederation. Those are the borders of Luxembourg today.

The same treaty bound the great powers to respect Belgian neutrality. Germany broke that promise in 1914, and the German chancellor called the treaty a scrap of paper, a phrase that helped bring Britain into the war.
sum: The Treaty of London of 1839 settled the break between Belgium and the Netherlands, and in doing so split Luxembourg in two.
